newsitem.title: CANADA: Champion shrs jump on Volvo bid.
newsitem.headline: Champion shrs jump on Volvo bid.

text.p: Shares in Champion Road Machinery Ltd rose in morning trading on Thursday in Toronto after the contruction unit of Sweden's AB Volvo said it will bid C$15 a share for the road building equipment company.
Analysts said the C$173 million bid, which Volvo Construction said will be recommended by Champion's board, should succeed easily.
"I think a C$15 bid, given the fact that the company is supportive, is likely to succeed," said Roger Dent, director of research at Yorkton Securities.
"It's certainly a very good premium to the company's historic trading," Dent added.
Champion's shares were up 4.10 to 14.60 on a turnover of 453,709 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange, well above the 52-week high of 11.25. The stock rose 2-3/4 to 10-5/8 in light trade on Nasdaq.

"I think it's a very good price. I think it's a fair value for the company," said a second analyst, who asked not to be identified. "As far as I'm concerned it will be done very easily and my feeling is everyone is going to tender."
Goderich, Ontario-based Champion could not immediately be reached for comment.
Analysts said a competing offer was possible but Volvo's bid would be hard to top.

"It's certainly possible that others could come out of the woodwork," said Dent. "(But) there's a significant, C$5 million penalty fee if somebody else ultimately buys the company, so anyone else buying the company is at a disadvantage because of that fee."
